files are in `data/`. Make a SINGLE attempt and produce the deliverable the

The directory data/ contains an events export (data/events.csv) and the data contract it must satisfy (data/contract.md). Some rows violate the contract.
Register a feature table named `events45bd4b`, version 1, on the platform, with record key `row_id` and event-time column `event_time` (epoch milliseconds), and load ONLY the rows that satisfy every contract rule.

The Databricks CLI is available as `databricks`. It is authenticated via DATABRICKS_HOST and DATABRICKS_TOKEN

Create everything inside your per-run namespace so it is isolated and cleaned up correctly:

- Prefix the NAME of any job, DLT pipeline, serving/vector-search endpoint, cluster, or Lakebase database
  instance you create with the MLPAB_DATABRICKS_PREFIX env var (e.g. `${MLPAB_DATABRICKS_PREFIX}_<your-name>`).
- Put any workspace notebooks/files and MLflow experiments under `/Users/<your-user>/${MLPAB_DATABRICKS_PREFIX}/`.

## Restrictions — everything runs on the platform, nothing runs locally

All real work (ingestion, transformation, joins, training, inference) MUST run
on the platform through the interface described above. The deliverable must
exist ON THE PLATFORM — grading reads it back through the platform's own read
paths, so a local file is worth nothing. Everything is already installed — you

import dlt
from pyspark.sql.functions import col

# Read the raw events
raw_events = spark.read.csv("file:/Workspace/Repos/${MLPAB_DATABRICKS_PREFIX}/task/data/events.csv", header=True, inferSchema=True)

valid_categories = ["grocery", "travel", "salary", "rent", "other"]

filtered_events = raw_events.filter(
    (col("amount").isNotNull()) &

)

    }
)

    }
)

dlt.apply_changes(

    keys=["row_id"],
    sequence_by=col("event_time"),
    apply_as_deletes=None,

)"}
